sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della situazione geopolitica tesa tra Iran e Israele, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sopra 19, il che indica un livello di incertezza elevato. Il DXY è in aumento, il che può indicare una riduzione dell'appetito per il rischio. Il prezzo del petrolio è in aumento, il che può alimentare le preoccupazioni sull'inflazione.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the tense geopolitical situation between Iran and Israel, with a negative impact on equity markets and increased demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX is above 19, indicating a high level of uncertainty. The DXY is rising, which may indicate a decrease in risk appetite. The oil price is increasing, which may fuel inflation concerns.

Il DXY è in aumento dello 0,18% a 98,99. Il TLT è in calo dello 0,25% a 86,70. L'oro è in calo dello 0,33% a $4776,40.
market_impact_summary.en: Equity markets are down, with the S&P 500 losing 0.62%. The VIX is up 0.31% to 19.43. The oil price is up 1.72% to $97.57. The DXY is up 0.18% to 98.99. The TLT is down 0.25% to 86.70. Gold is down 0.33% to $4776.40.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con un tono positivo. Il Nikkei giapponese ha registrato un aumento dell'1.8% a 56.924 punti, mentre lo Shanghai cinese ha guadagnato lo 0.5% a 4.000 punti. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.4% a 25.866 punti. Questi risultati potrebbero influenzare positivamente l'apertura dei mercati europei.

La giornata odierna si apre con un sentiment di risk-off. L'S&P 500 ha chiuso con un guadagno dello 0.6% a 6.800 punti. Il Dollar Index (DXY) ha registrato un aumento dello 0.2% a 99 punti. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, ha sceso dello 0.3% a 19 punti. I tassi di interesse continuano a essere monitorati: il TLT Bond USA a 20 anni ha perso lo 0.2% a 87 punti, mentre il rendimento del decennale USA è salito dello 0.1% al 4.3%. L'oro è sceso dello 0.3% a 4.800 dollari l'oncia.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la situazione rimane tesa. La Nato è divisa sull'accesso degli Usa alle basi europee in caso di guerra con l'Iran. Questo ha creato incertezza e potrebbe influenzare i mercati. Inoltre, la Cina sta aumentando i prezzi delle merci a causa della guerra in Iran, il che potrebbe avere un impatto sull'inflazione globale.

Sul fronte macroeconomico, l'attenzione si concentra sui dati in arrivo. Il PIL dell'Eurozona per il quarto trimestre è stato del 0.2%, in linea con le aspettative. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati, con il tasso sui depositi al 2%. Negli Usa, i dati storici mostrano un tasso di disoccupazione del 4.3% e un incremento dei Non-Farm Payrolls di 178.000 unità. La prossima uscita importante sarà il PIL Usa per il primo trimestre, previsto per il 29 aprile.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali...

Iniziamo con Bitcoin, che ha raggiunto quota 71.625 dollari, con un incremento dello 0.9%. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un deflusso netto di 94 milioni di dollari. Tecnicamente, il trend sembra ancora positivo, con gli investitori che continuano a monitorare i livelli di supporto e resistenza chiave.

Passando alle altcoin, Ethereum è stabile a 2.182 dollari, con un incremento dello 0.1%. Solana guadagna lo 0.9% a 83 dollari, mentre Binance Coin scende dello 0.1% a 599 dollari. Questi movimenti riflettono una certa stabilità nel mercato delle altcoin, con alcuni titoli che continuano a mostrare una buona resilienza.

L'indice Fear & Greed è a 16, in territorio di Extreme Fear. Questo livello suggerisce che gli investitori sono ancora molto cauti e che potrebbe esserci una maggiore volatilità nel breve termine. La correlazione con i dati macroeconomici, come l'inflazione e i tassi di interesse, rimane una variabile importante da monitorare.

In generale, il mercato delle criptovalute sembra essere in una fase di consolidamento, con alcuni titoli che continuano a mostrare una buona tenuta. Tuttavia, l'estrema cautela degli investitori, come evidenziata dall'indice Fear & Greed, suggerisce che potrebbe esserci una maggiore volatilità nel breve termine.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Restate sintonizzati per ulteriori aggiornamenti e analisi di mercato. Un saluto da Prais Alért, arrivederci e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is cautious, with a risk-off tone prevailing in the markets. This reflects concerns over geopolitical tensions and their potential impact on the economy.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. The S&P 500 is up 0.6% at 6800, while the STOXX 600 is up 0.3%. The NIKKEI closed up 1.8% at 56,924, and the HANG SENG up 0.4% at 25,866. On the currency front, the EUR/USD is trading at 1.2, up 0.2% on the day. The Dollar Index (DXY) is at 99, also up 0.2%. In commodities, BRENT oil is up 1.7% at $98, while GOLD is down 0.3% at $4800/oz. Bond yields are slightly up, with the US 10Y Yield at 4.3%, up 0.1%.

Key events today include rising tensions in the Middle East, which have led to an increase in oil prices. The situation is being closely monitored by investors, who are also awaiting further economic data releases. In the Eurozone, the focus is on the upcoming CPI and unemployment data. In the US, market participants are looking forward to the PCE Core YoY data release. Central bank officials are also in focus, with speeches from Christine Lagarde and others.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Starting with Bitcoin, we're seeing a steady price action around $71,625, up 0.9% on the day. The recent PCE inflation data didn't spark a significant reaction, but the $80K target remains in focus. Notably, Bitcoin ETFs experienced a daily net outflow of $94M, which could be a sign of short-term investor caution. Despite this, the overall sentiment around Bitcoin remains bullish, driven by recession risks and a weaker dollar.

Moving on to altcoins, we're seeing a mixed bag of performances. Ethereum is up 0.1% at $2,182, while Solana and BNB are up 0.9% and down 0.1% respectively. The altcoin market is awaiting a catalyst to drive the next leg of the rally.

In terms of market sentiment, the Fear & Greed Index is firmly in Extreme Fear territory at 16. This could be a contrarian buy signal for some investors. However, it's essential to keep in mind that sentiment can shift rapidly in the crypto market. Overall, the crypto market is taking a cautious approach ahead of key economic data releases and regulatory developments.

Thanks for tuning in. We'll be back tomorrow with another update. Keep an eye on market trends and we'll catch you then. A final word from Prais Alért. Have a great day and we'll talk to you soon.

articles.title: Update from the Battlefield: Drones, Distance, and Diminishing Returns for Russia
articles.snippet: Michael Kofman joins Ryan to unpack the current state of the Russo-Ukrainian War after his recent trip to the front. They examine how drone warfare has transformed the battlefield into a dispersed contest over a vast kill zone, why Russian infiltration tactics have failed to produce meaningful gains, and how Ukraine is working to close gaps in its strike capabilities. articles.title: What is Strategic Rivalry? Why Should We Care?
articles.snippet: The states most likely to draw America into its next major crisis or war are not unknowns. They are the usual suspects: The same handful of states that have threatened the United States repeatedly across decades. Interstate rivals have caused roughly 80 percent of history’s wars and the odds of any given rivalry ending peacefully are little better than a coin toss. Yet America’s key strategy documents since the 2017 National Security Strategy have used phrases like great power competition, interstate strategic competition, and strategic competition without acknowledging the essential difference between a competition and a rivalry. articles.title: Iran’s Asymmetric Counterair Campaign: Attacking the U.S. Air Force’s Nests and Eggs
articles.snippet: On March 27, Iranian drones and missiles struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia, destroying an E-3 Sentry, an airborne command center for U.S. operations in the region, and damaging multiple KC-135 tankers. It was not the first strike. Earlier in the month, an Iranian attack had already damaged five KC-135s at the same base. In the history of these aircraft, no enemy had ever achieved such a hit until Iran did both — within two weeks.These strikes are the latest in a broader pattern, part of a deliberate counterair campaign waged through asymmetric means in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. articles.title: Europe’s Gas Market Faces a Brutal Storage Refill Season
articles.snippet: Europe’s benchmark natural gas prices have eased from the three-year highs hit in March as reduced rates of withdrawal at the end of the heating season and news of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire calmed the extremely volatile gas market. But the European market appears too complacent as the real stress test for Europe’s gas supply will unfold in the coming months, analysts say. The European Commission has warned that energy prices will remain elevated for months to come, regardless of ceasefires or an immediate unconditional reopening…

articles.title: EU Eases Methane Rules to Keep Oil and Gas Flowing
articles.snippet: The European Union is preparing to loosen methane rules on imported oil and gas as the bloc scrambles to secure supply in the wake of the U.S.-Iran war. Brussels is set to introduce “flexibilities” to its methane regulations, allowing importers to comply without tracing emissions data back to individual cargoes. Instead, countries exporting to the EU will only need to show that a sufficient share of their national production meets the standards, according to the European Commission. articles.title: Strategy’s (MSTR) Bitcoin Ambition Is Reshaping Corporate Finance. Everyone Else Is Falling Behind
articles.snippet: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy’s (MSTR) Bitcoin Ambition Is Reshaping Corporate Finance. Everyone Else Is Falling Behind Michael Saylor’s Strategy is driving nearly all corporate Bitcoin accumulation, turning its STRC-fueled treasury model into the dominant force reshaping how companies approach Bitcoin in 2026. This post Strategy’s (MSTR) Bitcoin Ambition Is Reshaping Corporate Finance. Everyone Else Is Falling Behind first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .
